title: Implement hot/cold tiers for audit_events via range partitioning and compact projections
creator: Omar Williams
description: Large audit_events table is a hotspot for tenant reads and PG vacuum costs. This ticket introduces a hot/cold tier strategy: range-partition the table by event_timestamp into recent (hot) and historical (cold) partitions, create compact read-only projections for high-throughput API paths, and normalize duplicated JSONB blobs into a deduplicated events_payloads table. The goal is to reduce tail latency for tenant queries, lower index bloat, and make future TTL/prune operations efficient while maintaining zero-downtime for the control plane.
acceptance_criteria: Audit events table partitioned by month with current 90-day hot partitions and archived cold partitions older than 90 days
API read latency for tenant event queries reduced 40% p95 in staging for sample tenants
Reduced WAL and vacuum churn on cold partitions by at least 60% in synthetic load tests
No user-facing downtime or failed writes during migration; writes routed to partitioned parent table transparently
Compact projections (tenant_event_projections) populated and used by routes that require recent metadata only
Backfill and dedupe job completes within maintenance window for 90% of tenants; remainder queued for background reindexing
migration_plan: Step 0: Create design doc and validate on staging (Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/CP-Partitioning-HotCold)
Step 1: Add partitioned parent table audit_events_v2 with identical columns and partitioning by RANGE (event_timestamp)
Step 2: Deploy lightweight trigger that forwards inserts from audit_events to audit_events_v2 for a canary tenant set
Step 3: Run parallel reader tests against audit_events_v2 to validate query plans and index choices
Step 4: Create deduplicated events_payloads table and migrate unique JSONB payloads using chunked upserts
Step 5: Create tenant_event_projections (compact read-only view) populated via async materializer with low-latency replication
Step 6: Switch API read routes for non-critical paths to projections; run perf tests and iterate on indexes
Step 7: Gradually flip write traffic to partitioned table for all tenants using backfill sync and logical replication where necessary
Step 8: After verification, drop legacy indexes and alter audit_events to become a small routing shim that points at audit_events_v2
Step 9: Schedule periodic cold compaction jobs and set TTL pruning for partitions older than configured retention
rollback_plan: If reader regressions are detected, revert API routing to legacy table and disable forwarder trigger. For write regressions, pause write redirection and drain the canary queue. Keep a snapshot of audit_events_v2 and events_payloads to allow fast rollback to pre-migration state.
performance_metrics: Baseline p95 tenant event read latency: 220ms (prod sampling)
Target p95 after hot/cold split: <=130ms for recent-partition queries
WAL growth reduction target on cold partitions: 60%
Estimated index size reduction for hot partitions: 30%
notes: Trade-offs: Range partitioning simplifies TTL but increases complexity for cross-partition analytics. We prefer compact projections for analytics-lite routes to avoid full scans.
Index choices: Use btree on (tenant_id,event_timestamp) for hot partitions; consider BRIN for very large cold partitions to reduce index size.
Foreign keys: Temporarily relax FK constraints for bulk backfill to speed up migration; re-add with validated constraint once backfill completes.
Coordination: Will need an ops window for the heavy backfill and to monitor replica lag; notify SRE and Customer Success for tenants with high activity.
